title: Asset management plan and community benefit agreement review
subtitle: Also covered: employee engagement survey results, staff recognitions, a health accountability declaration and closed-session updates.
overview: The committee recommended that Council approve the 2025 Corporate Asset Management Plan, including targeted levels of service, for submission to the Ministry of Infrastructure by July 1, 2025 {{vote:m3}}. Staff said the plan sets targets that aim to stop the infrastructure backlog from getting worse, because current funding assumptions mean service levels are expected to decline. Tax-supported assets are not forecast to reach sustainable funding until around 2043.

It also recommended approving the changes from the Community Benefit Agreement Program Review {{vote:m2}}. These aim to make agreements with community partners clearer, more transparent and more accountable, with the city leading the process and tying agreements to the work needed.

The committee further recommended that the Mayor sign the annual Ontario Health Multi-Sector Service Accountability Agreement declaration of compliance {{vote:m4}}. It heard an employee engagement update and recognized three staff achievements. After a closed session, the Mayor reported that Council received information on enterprise risk management and gave staff direction on the Hanlon Creek Business Park and on 35, 45 and 55 Silvercreek Parkway.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council approve the plan and its targeted levels of service for submission to the Ministry of Infrastructure by July 1, 2025.
The committee recommended approving the staff recommendations to make community benefit agreements city-led, with clearer governance, budgeting, reporting and evaluation.
The committee recommended authorizing the Mayor to sign the Ontario Health Multi-Sector Service Accountability Agreement declaration of compliance for April 1, 2024 to March 31, 2025.

debate: On the asset plan, one councillor asked what "funding" means; staff said it mainly means infrastructure renewal funding, not development charges, and forecasts exclude surprise grants.
Staff said road pavement condition has improved with past investment, though the backlog and the decline in target service levels remain. Members discussed public concern about roads.
Several members said provincial and federal constraints and grants tied to new priorities make it hard to address the backlog; they favoured advocating for stable, predictable funding.
Councillors asked whether the city can deliver more capital work if funding rises. Staff said the organization is near capacity and the budget process is where those trade-offs get weighed.

On community benefit agreements, councillors asked about city board representation and access for smaller groups. Staff said board roles could be considered as agreements renew, and that the changes aim to reduce barriers through open, public processes.
